request.system:
You propose a draft theme taxonomy for recorded calls at Aegis Cloud Security (customer support calls, account manager calls with customers, internal meetings). The taxonomy is shared across all call types, so a theme must not be defined by the type of call.

Input: two independent discovery runs, each a consolidated list of candidate themes (source ids "r1.cN" and "r2.cN", with name, definition, owner and the number of calls each covers) and product areas, plus a scripted overlap table saying which run 1 and run 2 candidates cover mostly the same calls.

Task: propose a draft taxonomy "v0" of 6 to 8 themes.
- Prefer themes that both runs found (high overlap); a theme found by only one run needs a clear reason to stay.
- Each theme must pass the actionability test: one of "support lead", "sales / account manager", "product manager", "engineering lead" would act on a pattern of calls with that theme.
- Themes should be distinguishable from each other and together cover most calls. Keep an explicit "Other / new theme" bucket outside the 6 to 8.
- For each theme give: name (2 to 5 words), definition (one sentence), boundary_note (one sentence on how to tell it from its nearest neighbor), owner, sources (the r1/r2 ids it draws on), and note (why merged, or why kept despite being found in one run only; empty string if nothing to add).
- dropped_candidates: candidates you left out (or folded away), each with the source id and a one-sentence reason. Every candidate source id must appear in a theme's sources or in dropped_candidates.
- product_areas: the product names to use as a separate field, each with a one-sentence note. Merge variants and keep only products that the runs found with evidence.
- other_policy: one sentence on when a call goes to "Other / new theme" and what to do when that bucket grows.
- rationale: three sentences at most on how you chose the set.

Return only JSON matching the schema.

themes.name: Pipeline Outage Technical Remediation
themes.definition: Calls addressing the architectural investigation, failover engineering, and technical root-cause remediation of streaming ingestion and pipeline outages.
themes.boundary_note: Focuses strictly on engineering infrastructure stabilization and post-mortems rather than commercial SLA retention discussions or routine connector latency.
themes.note: Merges run 1 and run 2 engineering remediation topics that share the technical incident response call cluster.

themes.name: Commercial Renewals and Retention
themes.definition: Commercial discussions covering contract renewals, account expansions, multi-year commitments, SLA negotiations, and churn prevention following service disruptions.
themes.boundary_note: Focuses on commercial contract terms, packaging, and account retention rather than root-cause technical debugging or new deployment kickoffs.
themes.note: Consolidates standard renewals with post-outage SLA retention saves into a unified sales account preservation theme.

themes.name: Compliance Product Adoption and Expansion
themes.definition: Calls involving product previews, rollout readiness, feature demonstrations, and roadmap requests for multi-framework compliance reporting.
themes.boundary_note: Focuses on capability education and roadmap requests for compliance features rather than commercial contract negotiations or internal corporate audits.
themes.note: Combines Comply v2 adoption tracking with custom reporting framework expansion requests.

themes.name: Identity Authentication and Directory Provisioning
themes.definition: Calls concerning directory synchronization queues, SAML SSO regressions, session timeouts, and SCIM/IAM policy provisioning.
themes.boundary_note: Centers strictly on access control and directory sync troubleshooting rather than alert rule tuning or backup job infrastructure.
themes.note: Merged high-overlap identity access management topics across both discovery runs.

themes.name: Backup Performance and Scalability
themes.definition: Calls addressing degraded backup throughput, snapshot deduplication bottlenecks, connector permission failures, and restore limitations.
themes.boundary_note: Covers runtime degradation and storage failures in protection workflows rather than initial implementation architecture design.
themes.note: Unifies operational storage performance bottlenecks and backup failure candidate themes.

themes.name: Customer Implementation and Architecture Scoping
themes.definition: Structured onboarding, technical kickoff, and environment scoping sessions guiding new customers through initial policy and module deployment.
themes.boundary_note: Focuses on initial pre-production deployment architecture and milestones rather than post-launch break-fix troubleshooting or renewal discussions.
themes.note: Brings together implementation kickoff and deployment architecture candidate themes across both runs.

themes.name: Detection Alert Tuning and Optimization
themes.definition: Calls assisting customers with configuring behavioral baselines, suppressing false-positive spikes, and tuning detection thresholds to reduce SOC fatigue.
themes.boundary_note: Deals with rule sensitivity and baseline calibration during operational monitoring rather than total streaming pipeline outages.
themes.note: Captures recurring operational calls regarding rule noise calibration identified in both runs.

product_areas.name: Aegis Detect
product_areas.note: Platform module for threat detection, alert calibration, and high-throughput telemetry ingestion.

product_areas.name: Aegis Comply
product_areas.note: Platform module delivering multi-framework compliance auditing and scheduled reporting.

product_areas.name: Aegis Protect
product_areas.note: Platform module managing data backup jobs, snapshot deduplication, and restore orchestration.

product_areas.name: Aegis Identity
product_areas.note: Platform module managing directory synchronization, SSO authentication, and IAM provisioning.

dropped_candidates.reason: Exhibits negligible call volume and represents isolated post-launch bug triage that fits into standard product feedback or Other.
Internal competitive intelligence and battlecard reviews lack clear cross-run overlap and are better handled via internal sales strategy channels.
Overlaps minimally with pipeline remediation and SIEM egress buffering; subsumed into general infrastructure triage.
Egress connector buffer latencies are specific low-frequency connector issues that fold into general technical support.
One-off invoice consumption disputes are low-volume transactional billing inquiries best managed by general support.
Internal SOC 2 readiness meetings reflect internal operational overhead rather than cross-cutting call themes across customer and internal interactions.

parsed.other_policy: A call is routed to 'Other / new theme' when it entails routine one-off administrative check-ins, miscellaneous billing questions, or isolated internal discussions; if this bucket exceeds 10% of total volume, calls should be re-clustered to identify emerging product or operational categories.
parsed.rationale: Themes were selected by prioritizing core clusters that appeared across both runs with high overlap scores and distinct operational owners. Sub-scale themes such as isolated bug reports, internal SOC 2 reviews, and one-off overage disputes were dropped or consolidated to preserve clear boundaries. The resulting seven themes ensure comprehensive coverage across incident engineering, commercial lifecycle, compliance adoption, and core module support.
